// Room "P3 dormer bedroom" (interior designer's part): front bedroom behind the long shed dormer, one bed.
// Inner air x 58..60, z 14..16, feet y 6 (floor block y 5, ceiling y 9). The bed is the focal piece: its head is against
// the east wall (x 61), so it sits where the doorway (west, x 57) looks. Chest dresser by the foot, a spruce-fence table
// with a top slab and a flower pot, one stair chair, and a standing lantern on a fence post for the light.
import { layers, bed } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // the bed: foot (59,6,14), head (60,6,14) against the east wall, both halves via bed()
  bed(g, [59, 6, 14], "east", "red");

  // feet level (y 6): chest dresser at (58,14); chair stairs at (58,16) facing the table; table post and lantern post at z16
  layers(g, [58, 6, 14], {
    c: ["chest", { facing: "east", type: "single" }],
    s: ["spruce_stairs", { facing: "east", half: "bottom", shape: "straight" }],
    f: ["spruce_fence", {}],
  }, [
    ["c  ", "   ", "sff"],
  ]);

  // y 7: the table top slab (top half, sits on the post) and the standing lantern on the lantern post
  layers(g, [58, 7, 14], {
    t: ["spruce_slab", { type: "top" }],
    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
  }, [
    ["   ", "   ", " tL"],
  ]);

  // y 8: a potted flower on the table top
  layers(g, [58, 8, 14], {
    p: ["potted_poppy", {}],
  }, [
    ["   ", "   ", " p "],
  ]);
}

parts/room-28.mjs (P3 dormer bedroom) now places its bed at z15 (foot 59,6,15, head 60,6,15) with the chest at 58,6,15 and the chair, table and lantern as before.
make.sh exits 0 and writes build.nbt; this part reports placed 9, refused 0, offPalette none.
The old bed and chest sat in z14, which is the dormer's solid underside (deepslate_tiles), so the bed was silently skipped and the chest was refused.
left: Dormer geometry: cell 60,8,14 is open floor under the roof slope and unreachable from the room (mcd room: 4 of 5 floor cells reached). Not this part's to fix; the roof/dormer part would need to clear it or the room would need to drop that cell.
The room's z14 row is now solid roof material, so the room is effectively x58..60 z15..16. The rooms.json box (z14..16) and the plan.md note still describe z14 as floor.

waste.what: Found which earlier part owned the refused cell and what was at each cell in the room by writing a throwaway probe script that loads build.nbt and prints block names over x57..61, y5..9, z13..17.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one probe script, to read 25 cells per level
waste.tool: mcd cells build.nbt --box 57,5,13,61,9,17 (or a --owner flag that names the part that wrote each cell) would show the state and owner of every cell in one call.

waste.what: A bed() call that hits occupied cells returns false and writes nothing, and that failure is not counted in the refused list, so the bed vanished with no error. I only found it by checking the cells afterward.
waste.cost: one extra build and a probe to notice the bed was missing (parts-report showed only the chest)
waste.tool: bed() (and the other b-helpers) should add refused entries for their cells, the way g.set does, so parts-report.json lists the bed as well as the chest.

waste.what: Picked the new bed and chest cells by hand from the probe grid: the head/foot/lane rules, and which cells above each half are clear.
waste.cost: about 4 cells checked by hand, plus a second full make.sh run to confirm
waste.tool: mcd plan build.nbt --rooms rooms.json run before the room parts (after the roof) would print the free cells for each room, so the designer picks a bed site from free cells instead of the planned ones.

waste.what: The room's header and rooms.json box assumed z14 was floor, but the shed dormer's solid underside takes it. The conflict only showed up in the refusal report after a full build.
waste.cost: one full build cycle lost to the wrong floor plan
waste.tool: A pre-room check (mcd plan on the shell+roof stage) that flags room box cells already solid, so the planner sees the roof has taken z14 before a designer writes a bed there.

companions.task: Check whether the shed dormer's solid underside at z14, y6..8 (roof material on the shell) can be cut back to give the room its full 3-deep floor. That would let the bed and chest go back to the planned z14 site, and would clear the unreachable 60,8,14 cell.
